_comment: Screen recordings the videos would use if they existed. Until a clip with this id is registered (scripts/register_source.py) every scene falls back to the real screenshot named in its 'fallback' field.

early-factory.show: First launch: the tutorial card 'This is your factory', tap Open factory, the first Small Car Body Works producing, first money ticking up.

early-small-body-works.show: The Small Car Body Works panel (LV 1): buy steel, 'Producing' status, first cars made.

expansion-build.show: Real expansion: Build menu → buy land → place a new factory → it starts producing. Then upgrade a plant (level up).

factory-interior.show: Inside the Car Assembly Plant in portrait: slow camera along the conveyor, workers moving, cars appearing. Use the TOUR button if it gives a nice camera.

factory-interior-2.show: A second pass through a plant (landscape or portrait): Body store → Powertrain marriage → Trim line → Wheels → Paint and finish.

factory-finished.show: The end of the line: Quality control → Finished cars, '+8' pop-ups.

map-traffic.show: The city map: trucks driving between plants, day or night, slow camera drift. Try one daytime and one night take.

map-overview.show: Zoom out to the whole empire: many factories, floating income numbers (+$17.2K).

map-dealers.show: Dealers on the map and cash popping up.

car-models.show: Models & Design: scroll models, change paint / open the garage.

racing.show: A race in the Racing District (or the race list scrolling).

research.show: Research Lab: buy a technology, scroll to Electric.

how_to_record: Use a real phone or the Android emulator. Portrait, 1080x1920 (or the phone's native 9:16).
Android 11+: swipe down → 'Screen record'. Or from a PC: adb shell screenrecord --size 1080x1920 --bit-rate 16000000 --time-limit 30 /sdcard/clip.mp4 && adb pull /sdcard/clip.mp4
Turn on Do Not Disturb, hide notifications and personal data (use a clean save). Keep the game's own sound off – the pipeline adds its own music.
Record 2-3 seconds longer than needed at the start and end; move the camera slowly.
Save as assets/gameplay/clips/<clip id>.mp4, then: python scripts/register_source.py assets/gameplay/clips/<clip id>.mp4 --id <clip id> --real --description "..."
Re-run python scripts/render.py all – scenes automatically use the registered clip instead of the screenshot.
